title: Apremilast attenuates methotrexate-induced hepatic injury in rats; insights into TLR4/NF-kappaB/P38 MAPK/caspase-3 and alpha-klotho/Nrf2/HO-1 signaling network interplay.
authors: Mohyeldin, Reham H; Sharata, Ehab E; Abdelnaser, Mahmoud; Ibrahim, Ayman M; Attya, Mina Ezzat; Kotb, Al Shaimaa Mahmoud; S Aboalela, Ahmed; Rofaeil, Remon Roshdy
one_liner_zh: 该研究探讨阿普斯特对甲氨蝶呤诱导大鼠肝损伤的保护机制，聚焦信号通路与组织病理，不涉及蛋白质-DNA互作或AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: AIM: This study aimed to assess the preventive potential of apremilast (APRE) against methotrexate (MTX)-induced hepatotoxicity through modulation of Nrf2/HO-1 and TLR4/NF-kappaB/p38 MAPK/Caspase-3 pathways. MAIN METHODS: Male rats were assigned to the control, apremilast, methotrexate, and methotrexate + apremilast groups. Histopathological investigation and analysis of the serum hepatotoxicity indicators (AST, ALT, ALP, and GGT) were used to evaluate the hepatic toxicity. Testing for hepatic MDA and GSH was conducted. The levels of hepatic TNF-alpha, IL-6, Nrf2, alpha-klotho, HO-1, and cleaved caspase-3 were measured using the ELISA method. Using an immunohistochemistry method, the expression of NF-kappaB p65 was investigated. Western blotting was used to examine the expression of TLR4 and p38 MAPK, and docking experiments were performed on all proteins that were investigated. KEY FINDINGS: The liver was significantly affected, as evidenced by higher levels of ALT, AST, ALP, and GGT as well as increased levels of hepatic MDA, TNF-alpha, IL-6, BAX, Caspase-3, and decreased GSH activity and BCL-2 expression. These outcomes were linked to inhibition of alpha-klotho/Nrf2/HO-1 signaling and activation of TLR4/NF-kappaB/p38 MAPK/Caspase-3. Co-treatment with APRE markedly improved all biochemical and pathological alterations evoked by MTX. CONCLUSION: Apremilast mitigates the harmful effects of methotrexate on the liver by activating signaling cascades that include Nrf2/HO-1, while downregulating TLR4/NF-kappaB/p38 MAPK/Caspase-3.
abstract_zh: 目的：本研究旨在评估阿普斯特（APRE）通过调节Nrf2/HO-1和TLR4/NF-kappaB/p38 MAPK/Caspase-3通路对甲氨蝶呤（MTX）诱导的肝毒性的预防潜力。主要方法：雄性大鼠被分为对照组、阿普斯特组、甲氨蝶呤组和甲氨蝶呤+阿普斯特组。通过组织病理学检查及血清肝毒性指标（AST、ALT、ALP和GGT）分析来评估肝脏毒性。检测了肝脏MDA和GSH水平。使用ELISA方法测量了肝脏TNF-alpha、IL-6、Nrf2、alpha-klotho、HO-1和cleaved caspase-3的水平。采用免疫组织化学方法研究了NF-kappaB p65的表达。使用Western blotting检测TLR4和p38 MAPK的表达，并对所有研究的蛋白质进行了对接实验。主要发现：肝脏受到显著影响，表现为ALT、AST、ALP和GGT水平升高，以及肝脏MDA、TNF-alpha、IL-6、BAX、Caspase-3水平增加，GSH活性和BCL-2表达降低。这些结果与alpha-klotho/Nrf2/HO-1信号通路抑制及TLR4/NF-kappaB/p38 MAPK/Caspase-3激活相关。与APRE联合治疗显著改善了MTX引起的所有生化和病理改变。结论：阿普斯特通过激活包括Nrf2/HO-1在内的信号级联反应，同时下调TLR4/NF-kappaB/p38 MAPK/Caspase-3，减轻了甲氨蝶呤对肝脏的有害影响。
